rulings.why: 'Behold, I will punish Amon of No' (JER 46:25): אמון here is the god Amon of Thebes, and No, the next word, is the city; the word was held on the city.

Pashhur's other name, which the project owner (2026-11-01) asked to be read: 'The LORD hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magormissabib' (JER 20:3). The name is H4036 מָגוֹר מִסָּבִיב, written מָגוֹר מִ סָּבִיב: the first and the last word carry it. The same מָגוֹר in JER 6:25, 20:10, 46:5 and 49:29 is the common 'terror on every side' and is not this name.

Pashhur's other name, which the project owner (2026-11-01) asked to be read: 'The LORD hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magormissabib' (JER 20:3). The name is H4036 מָגוֹר מִסָּבִיב, written מָגוֹר מִ סָּבִיב: the first and the last word carry it. The same מָגוֹר in JER 6:25, 20:10, 46:5 and 49:29 is the common 'terror on every side' and is not this name.
'Not Pashur but Metoikon' (JER 20:3): the Greek gives Pashhur's other name, Magor-missabib, by its sense, a sojourner, and the word stands where the name stands.
Naomi's other name, given in the verse: 'Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me' (RUT 1:20). מָרָא (H4755) is the name, and no text carried it.
'And he called his name Jedidiah' (2SA 12:25): the Greek's spelling of Solomon's other name, which the Hebrew's יְדִידְיָהּ carries and no text of the Septuagint did.
'And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnath-paaneah' (GEN 41:45): the Greek's spelling of the name Pharaoh gave Joseph, which the Hebrew's צָפְנַת פַּעְנֵחַ carries and no text of the Septuagint did.
